content.text:
## Audit

I read through `index.html` (structure, styles, and both inline scripts). The markup already uses semantic, native elements throughout: real `<label>`s correctly paired via `for`/`id`, a real `<button type="submit">` for the primary action, and plain `<input>` elements — no custom widgets, no ARIA retrofits needed. Color contrast (button, subtext, note text) all comfortably exceeds WCAG AA thresholds, and no CSS strips the default focus outline, so focus is visible everywhere.

The one defect I found: every form control had an explicit, out-of-order `tabindex` (`3, 1, 2, 5, 4` on first-name, last-name, email, party-size, and the submit button respectively). That scrambles keyboard tab order into Last name → Email → First name → Book → Party size, which doesn't match the visual reading order and violates WCAG 2.4.3 (Focus Order) — a keyboard-only user would fill the form in a confusing, mismatched sequence.

## Fix

Removed the `tabindex` attributes from all five controls. The underlying DOM order (First name → Last name → Email → Party size → Book the table) already matches the visual layout exactly, so letting the browser use natural document order restores a correct, predictable tab sequence with zero markup/behavior changes otherwise.

## Left alone

- The `data-track` attributes, `id`s, and the click-instrumentation script — untouched, as required.
- The submit `preventDefault()` handler — untouched.
- All native elements — button/inputs/labels kept as-is since they already satisfy the "custom-styled widget stays native/custom" rule; no design changes were needed.
- Verified the real `<button>` still fires a genuine `click` event on keyboard activation (Enter/Space while focused), so `window.__activated` behaves identically for mouse and keyboard users.

The page now has a correct, logical keyboard tab order matching its visual design, with no other accessibility defects found (labels, contrast, focus visibility, and semantics were already sound).
